html:
The Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, the Iran nuclear deal, was signed in Vienna on 14 July 2015 by Iran with the United States, Britain, France, Germany, Russia, China and the European Union.

Iran agreed to cut its stock of enriched uranium, limit its centrifuges and accept close inspections, so that it could not quickly build a bomb. In return, international sanctions on its oil and banks were lifted in 2016.

In May 2018 President Donald Trump withdrew the United States and brought back sanctions. Iran then enriched uranium far beyond the limits. In June 2025 Israel and the United States bombed Iran's nuclear sites, and later that year the European parties restored the UN sanctions. See also Iranian Revolution and Iran.
sum: The Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, the Iran nuclear deal, was signed in Vienna on 14 July 2015 by Iran with the United States, Britain, France, Germany, Russia, China and the European Union.
